newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to cut costs at Gullfaks.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to cut costs at Gullfaks.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday a new approach to operating Gullfaks B had been approved by the licensees for this North Sea field to cut production costs.
"Production profiles show that full transfer of unprocessed wellstreams from the B platform to Gullfaks A or C could be relevant from 2001," Status Weekly newsletter said.
That would convert Gullfaks B into a pure wellhead platform, with only as many crew as are required to operate and maintain the wellstream equipment," it said.
Status Weekly said a project team appointed by Statoil to prepare for this form of operation would plan an intermediate phase with low staffing of the platform.
Project manager Tor Arne Haugen said low staffing was due to start on August 1 next year. Each Gullfaks B shift will then be cut from today's 66 crew to 48, freeing 42 people for other duties.
"Extending the period of profitable operation for as long as possible is the ultimate aim," the report said.
